choose-work.text: Select the next attempt to pursue an intention.

C01.text: Only the steward chooses subsequent work after any ended attempt.

meta.rationale: The single-owner rule avoids ambiguous responsibility for choosing the next attempt.

C02.text: After a failed attempt, choosing among next-work alternatives belongs to the steward.

meta.rationale: This applies the universal steward choice rule to failure.

C03.text: Operator approval alone does not let an orchestrator independently choose replacement work after failure.

meta.rationale: The retired bypass avoided a relay, but preserving one owner for next-work selection won out.

C04.text: After retries are exhausted, selecting the next attempt goes back to the steward.

meta.rationale: This failure branch inherits the same responsibility boundary.

C05.text: A replacement after a failed investigation needs a plan selected by the steward.

meta.rationale: Both the failed-replacement boundary and exhausted-retry handoff support this conclusion.

C06.text: The orchestrator handles recoverable worker blockers within its current authority.

meta.rationale: Execution recovery need not change the intended work.

C07.text: An intention persists when one attempted record fails.

meta.rationale: A failed realization does not erase the original concern.

C08.text: Every completed linked record makes its intention available for steward reassessment.

meta.rationale: A simple wake rule avoids losing branch completions.

C09.text: The desk is an interface for items whose next action belongs to the operator.

meta.rationale: Ownership names the next action owed.

C10.text: Starting an agent session and permitting it to continue autonomously are separate decisions.

meta.rationale: User launch does not imply user-driven execution.

Q01.text: Must the orchestrator ask the operator before stopping a degraded attempt?

Q02.text: Which arbitrary cancellation outcomes should wake the steward?

S01.text: SYNTHETIC prior accepted decision: the steward always chooses the next work after an attempt ends. Reason: one owner is easier to understand and holds responsibility across records.

S02.text: SYNTHETIC history: an operator-approved orchestrator replacement exception was considered because the orchestrator already held the failure context and a relay could be wasteful. It was withdrawn in favor of the single-owner steward rule. This source records the earlier debate, not a current permission.

S03.text: SYNTHETIC prior context: execution recovery, durable intentions, completion wakeups, desk ownership and start-versus-drive are accepted as individually listed. Whether stopping always requires consultation remains open. Arbitrary cancellation policy remains open.
